args.subtitle: Split every rupee, and the month plans itself
rows: 50% Needs — rent, groceries, fuel, bills, minimum debt payments
30% Wants — dining out, subscriptions, shopping, travel
20% Savings — emergency fund, investments, extra debt payoff

args.title: Renting vs. Buying
args.subtitle: Two ways to pay for a home
rows: Renting — A monthly payment buys only the use of someone else's home. No equity builds, and it resets the moment you move.
Buying — Part of every payment builds equity you keep, even after you sell.

Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now.
Five Steps to Launch
args.subtitle: From first customer conversation to compounding growth
rows: Research — Talk to customers, size the real problem, and name who pays for it
Prototype — Build the smallest version that proves the idea can work at all
Test — Put it in front of real users and fix what breaks before it ships
Launch — Ship to an audience you own, with the story already written
Grow — Double down on the channel that worked, then make retention carry it

args.title: 4 rules for writing hooks
rows: Be specific — name the exact number, tool or outcome, never 'most people'
Open a loop — pose the question the video answers in the first 3 seconds
Promise a payoff — tell them what they'll know or be able to do by the end
Cut the intro — no context, no credentials, no 'hey guys'; start on the payoff
